definition: Predicting the sequence of eye fixations a human will make when viewing an image, modeling visual attention over time.
details: Predicting the sequence of eye fixations a human will make when viewing an image, modeling visual attention over time.

explainer.lead: Scanpath prediction models the order in which a person's eyes move across an image, not just where they look. It matters for interfaces, advertising, and rendering where the sequence of attention drives comprehension.

tiers.eli5: It predicts the path your eyes will take across a picture, like guessing the route of a bouncing ball before it moves.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to evaluate layouts and compress or prioritize image regions in viewing order; a common pitfall is that individual scanpaths vary widely, so a single predicted sequence can be misleading.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, it outputs an ordered sequence of fixation coordinates (x, y, t) conditioned on an image, often modelled as a probability distribution over sequences. Limits: sequential metrics like string-edit distance penalize small spatial deviations heavily, and human scanpaths are highly variable.

explainer.example: Given a product webpage, the model predicts fixations moving logo, then headline, then price, in that order.
